concept.name: Post-only order
concept.definition: A limit order with an instruction that it may only add liquidity to the order book: if it would execute immediately against a resting order (i.e., would 'take' liquidity), it is instead canceled or repriced one tick away from the market. It guarantees the trader acts as a maker, avoiding taker fees and often earning liquidity rebates.
concept.intuition: Post-only is 'join the queue or don't trade at all' - you will never cross the spread, so you control fees and avoid paying for immediacy.
concept.mechanics: The venue checks the order's limit price against the opposite side of the book on arrival; a marketable post-only order is rejected/canceled or slid to a non-marketable price depending on venue rules. It then rests at its limit, earning maker treatment if executed against. On derivatives platforms (e.g., Bybit) it is expressed as timeInForce = PostOnly.
concept.failure_modes: In a fast-moving market the order may be canceled or slid repeatedly and never rest at an executable price, so the trader misses the move entirely. Repricing-by-venue variants can also post at a price different from the one intended.
concept.misconceptions: Post-only does not guarantee a fill or a rebate - it only guarantees that any execution that occurs will be as liquidity provider. Cancel-on-marketability and reprice-on-marketability are different venue behaviors, not one universal rule.
concept.example: With the book at $10.00 x $10.02, you submit a post-only buy at $10.02; because it would lift the offer immediately, the venue cancels it (or posts it at $10.01), ensuring you never pay the taker fee.
